text:
sam: quick design sync — attaching a tiny prototype (gif) that toggles between full-bleed rows and card-tiles for the model compare table. Link: https://imgur.com/fakegif. Looking for quick takes on density, keyboard nav, and pin CTA wording.

lio: cards read better when you have 5+ versions. visual groups help scan. downside = more vertical scroll. also: watch shadow vs border contrast at small sizes.

anya: from accessibility POV tiles introduce extra focusable regions. prefer a single row container with internal semantics so keyboard users can arrow through rows, not each inner control by default. recommend `role=\"row\"` with one primary focus target per row and use roving tabindex.

sam: good — proposal: row has one anchor focus area and pressing Enter opens a flyout with actions (pin, compare, metrics). does that match patterns we already use elsewhere?

tom: that matches the quick-actions pattern in model detail. flyout should be dismissible via Esc and click-away. for performance badges, let's fix column width and right-align so numbers don't jump.

lio: about pin microcopy: current hover title says "Pin". UX suggests slightly longer: "Pin this version". For screen readers, explicit toggle text: "Pin model to compare view."

anya: prefer toggle labels that include action + target: "Pin model to compare" / "Unpin model from compare". also add `aria-pressed` and update `aria-live` region when state changes so SR users hear confirmation.

sam: small UX question — should pin persist across sessions? if yes, we need to clarify scope in tooltip: "Pinned (this browser)" vs "Pinned (account)". thoughts?

tom: pins should be account-scoped. users expect cross-device persistence for saved views. Tooltip could say "Pinned to your account" on hover. Keep toast copy short: "Pinned to compare" (2s).

lio: badges legend — +1 for a keyboard-focusable legend icon in header. it should open a small dialog with thresholds and method: e.g., latency <120ms = green; 120-400ms = yellow; >400ms = red. include textual thresholds for screen reader.

anya: ensure color-blind accessible patterns: don't rely on color alone — add icon + text label for critical badges. also ensure the legend is reachable via skiplinks.

sam: design note — in dense mode we collapse metric labels and show only icons; expand-on-hover for accessibility. Concern: hover-only reveals are inaccessible. So make expand-on-focus too.

tom: focus outline — current 3px brand blue is slightly thick in compact tables; maybe 2px solid + subtle shadow. run contrast check vs bg.

a11y-bot: checklist: 1) roving tabindex implemented, 2) aria-pressed on pin toggle, 3) legend dialog with role=dialog & aria-label, 4) focus order tested with screen reader, 5) color + icon for badges.

sam: ok will update figma with tiles and full-bleed variants and include an accessibility sheet with required attributes. I'll open a PR and tag @anya and @lio for final sign-off. react with :thumbsup: for tiles, :eyes: for full-bleed. collecting reactions in 30m. thanks!
